89.s: Which device does Rule 198 of the Lok Sabha Rules govern?
89.x: Rule 198 (LS) – No-confidence motion

89.s: Which motion is governed by Rule 222 (LS) and Rule 187 (RS)?
89.x: Rule 222 (LS) / Rule 187 (RS) – Privilege motion

89.s: Which discussion deals with a matter already debated whose answer needs factual elucidation?
89.x: Half-an-hour discussion: a matter already sufficiently debated whose answer needs factual elucidation; the Speaker can allot 3 days a week; no formal motion or vote.

89.s: Since when has the short-duration discussion been in use in the Lok Sabha?
89.x: Short-duration discussion – 1953

89.s: What is a formal proposal by a member for the decision of the House called?
89.x: Motion – A formal proposal by a member for the decision of the House (to do something permissible); no discussion on a matter of public importance except on a motion with the Presiding Officer's consent

89.s: Which kind of motion is self-contained, such as an impeachment motion?
89.x: Kinds – Substantive (self-contained, e.g. impeachment), substitute, subsidiary (ancillary, superseding, amendment)

89.s: What is the aim of a privilege motion moved when a Minister withholds or distorts facts?
89.x: Privilege motion – Moved when a Minister withholds facts of a case or gives wrong / distorted facts – breach of privilege; aim: censure the minister; either House; referred to the Committee of Privileges; does not force the Government to resign

89.s: What kind of motion is a resolution always?
89.x: Always a substantive motion; the mover cannot withdraw it except by leave of the House; the same subject is barred for one year.

89.s: On which days are private members' resolutions taken up?
89.x: Private member's – Alternate Fridays, afternoon sitting

89.s: By whom is a Government resolution moved?
89.x: Government – Moved by a minister – treaties, policies, committee recommendations

89.s: What is a resolution moved under a constitutional or legal provision called?
89.x: Statutory – Moved under a constitutional or statutory provision

89.s: Which type of resolution is moved under a provision of the Constitution or an Act?
89.x: Statutory – Moved under a constitutional or statutory provision

89.s: What is the basis of the office of the Whip in India?
89.x: Basis – Outside the Constitution, the Rules and statute – rests on parliamentary conventions

89.s: In which year was the Leaders and Chief Whips of Recognised Parties and Groups in Parliament (Facilities) Act passed?
89.x: 1998 Act – Leaders and Chief Whips of Recognised Parties and Groups in Parliament (Facilities) Act – gives only facilities

89.s: Which parties in Parliament have their own whips?
89.x: Parties – Every party – ruling or opposition – has its own whips

89.s: Who is the Government Chief Whip in the Lok Sabha?
o: Leader of the House in the Rajya Sabha
89.x: Government Chief Whip (LS) – The (Cabinet) Minister of Parliamentary Affairs – keeps contact with the Chief Whips of parties in both Houses

89.s: What can a member face for defying the party whip?
89.x: Defying the whip – Disqualification under the Tenth Schedule

89.s: What is the nature of a one-line whip?
89.x: One-line – Informative

89.s: What does a two-line whip direct members to do?
89.x: Two-line – Direction to attend

89.s: What does a three-line whip direct members to do?
o: Vote strictly as the party directs
89.x: Three-line – Vote strictly as the party directs

89.s: Which motion is moved when a Minister gives wrong or distorted facts to the House?
89.x: Privilege motion – Moved when a Minister withholds facts of a case or gives wrong / distorted facts – breach of privilege

89.s: To which committee is a privilege motion referred?
89.x: Privilege motion – effect – Purpose: censure the minister; either House; referred to the Committee of Privileges; does not force the Government to resign

90.s: Which Article calls the Budget the Annual Financial Statement?
90.x: Constitutional name – Annual Financial Statement (AFS), Article 112 – estimated receipts and expenditure of the Government of India for that year

90.s: From which French word, meaning little bag, does the word "Budget" come?
90.x: Word "Budget" – Nowhere in the Constitution (Annual Financial Statement, Appropriation Bill and Consolidated Fund of India are); from French "bougette" = little bag

90.s: Before which body does the President cause the Annual Financial Statement to be laid?
90.x: Laid by – The President "causes" the AFS to be laid before both Houses; the Finance Minister presents it in the Lok Sabha (Union Budget 2023-24: Nirmala Sitharaman)

90.s: What is the financial year of the Government of India?
90.x: Financial year – 1 April – 31 March; Revenue Budget + Capital Budget; charged and voted expenditure shown separately (Art. 112(2))

90.s: In which month is the Budget Circular usually issued, starting Budget preparation?
90.x: Prepared by – Budget Division, Department of Economic Affairs (DEA), Ministry of Finance; starts with the Budget Circular (usually September)

90.s: Where is the Halwa ceremony, marking the start of Budget printing, held?
90.x: Halwa ceremony – North Block – start of the secrecy/printing of Budget documents

90.s: Which document is presented by the Finance Ministry a day or so before the Budget?
90.x: Economic Survey – Finance Ministry (DEA); presented before the Budget (a day or a few days earlier)

90.s: Under which Lok Sabha rule can the Budget be presented in two or more parts?
90.x: Budget in parts – Rule 213 (LS Rules) – in two or more parts, each dealt with as the Budget; Rule 204 fixes the day of presentation (no discussion that day)

90.s: Which Article deals with the Annual Financial Statement?
90.x: 112 – Annual Financial Statement; 112(3) charged items

90.s: Under which Article are estimates presented as Demands for Grants?
90.x: 113 – Estimates as Demands for Grants; only LS votes; Art. 113(3) President's recommendation

90.s: Which Article deals with the Appropriation Bill?
90.x: 114 – Appropriation Bill; 114(3) no withdrawal except under appropriation by law

90.s: Which Article deals with supplementary, additional and excess grants?
90.x: 115 – Supplementary, additional, excess grants

90.s: Which Article provides for vote on account, vote of credit and exceptional grants?
90.x: 116 – Vote on account, vote of credit, exceptional grants

90.s: Which Article deals with Financial Bills needing the President's recommendation?
90.x: 117 – Financial Bills (President's recommendation)

90.s: Which Article says no tax shall be levied except by authority of law?
90.x: 265 – No tax except by authority of law

90.s: Which article: Consolidated Fund & Public Account / Contingency Fund?
90.x: 266 / 267 – Consolidated Fund & Public Account / Contingency Fund

90.s: When was the first Budget of independent India presented?
90.x: First Budget of independent India – 26 Nov 1947, R.K. Shanmukham Chetty – the first Finance Minister (John Mathai 2nd, C.D. Deshmukh 3rd)

90.s: From which year was the Union Budget presented at 11 a.m. instead of 5 p.m.?
90.x: Time of presentation – 5 p.m. (colonial) → 11 a.m. from 2001 (Yashwant Sinha)

90.s: In which year was the Railway Budget separated from the General Budget?
90.x: Railway Budget – Separated 1924 (Acworth Committee, 1921); merged in 2017; first combined Budget by Arun Jaitley, 1 Feb 2017

90.s: From which year has the Union Budget been presented on 1 February?
90.x: Budget date – 1 February from 2017 (earlier the last working day of February)

90.s: In which year were the Outcome Budget and Gender Budget Statement first presented?
90.x: Outcome Budget / Gender Budget Statement – First in 2005-06

90.s: On which date in March 2012 did Pranab Mukherjee present the Union Budget 2012-13?
90.x: Union Budget 2012-13 – Presented 16 March 2012 (Pranab Mukherjee)

90.s: Which fund of Rs 1 lakh crore did the Union Budget 2026-27 propose?
90.x: Union Budget 2026-27 – 1 Feb 2026; proposed an Economic Stabilisation Fund of Rs 1 lakh crore

90.s: Which Finance Minister presented the Andhra Pradesh Budget 2026-27 on 14 Feb 2026?
90.x: AP Budget 2026-27 – 14 Feb 2026, FM Payyavula Keshav; separate agriculture budget by K. Atchannaidu – AP is one of the few States with a separate Agriculture Budget

90.s: Who presented the Interim Budget 2019-20 with its 'Vision 2030'?
90.x: Interim Budget 2019-20 – Piyush Goyal, 1 Feb 2019 – 'Vision 2030' with ten dimensions; the first: infrastructure for a USD 10 trillion economy

90.s: Into which fund do all revenues, loans and loan repayments of the Union go?
90.x: Receipts – All revenues (taxes and other receipts), all loans (Treasury Bills, ways and means advances), loan repayments – Money held in trust: provident funds, small savings, judicial deposits, savings bank deposits, remittances – Imprest for unforeseen expenditure

90.s: Which fund of the Union is an imprest for unforeseen expenditure?
90.x: Receipts – All revenues (taxes and other receipts), all loans (Treasury Bills, ways and means advances), loan repayments – Money held in trust: provident funds, small savings, judicial deposits, savings bank deposits, remittances – Imprest for unforeseen expenditure

90.s: How can money be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund of India?
o: Only under appropriation made by law
90.x: Withdrawal – Only under appropriation made by law – Parliament's authorisation (Art. 266(3), 114) – Executive action, no vote of Parliament (banking transactions) – Advance by the President, before Parliament's approval

90.s: How is money withdrawn from the Public Account of India?
o: By executive action, no vote of Parliament
90.x: Withdrawal – Only under appropriation made by law – Parliament's authorisation (Art. 266(3), 114) – Executive action, no vote of Parliament (banking transactions) – Advance by the President, before Parliament's approval

90.s: How is money drawn from the Contingency Fund of India?
90.x: Withdrawal – Only under appropriation made by law – Parliament's authorisation (Art. 266(3), 114) – Executive action, no vote of Parliament (banking transactions) – Advance by the President, before Parliament's approval

90.s: Who controls the Consolidated Fund of India?
90.x: Controlled by – Parliament – Executive – President; held by the Finance Secretary, DEA

90.s: Who controls the Public Account of India?
90.x: Controlled by – Parliament – Executive – President; held by the Finance Secretary, DEA

90.s: Who has the Contingency Fund of India at his disposal?
90.x: Controlled by – Parliament – Executive – President; held by the Finance Secretary, DEA

90.s: Which Article, read with Art. 114(3), requires an Appropriation Act to withdraw from the CFI?
90.x: Withdrawal from the CFI – Authorisation by Parliament (an Appropriation Act) – Art. 266(3) read with Art. 114(3); Ministries draw under the Appropriation Act

90.s: Which power over the issue of money does the CAG in India lack?
90.x: CAG – Has no "comptroller" power over issue of money in India; audits all three funds of the Union and the States

90.s: By which Act was the Contingency Fund of India created?
90.x: Contingency Fund of India – Created by Parliament by law – Contingency Fund of India Act, 1950; at the President's disposal; advances for unforeseen (also additional/excess) expenditure pending authorisation by Parliament

90.s: What is the corpus of the Contingency Fund of India since 2021-22?
90.x: Corpus – Rs 30,000 crore from 2021-22 (Rs 500 crore from 2005; Rs 50 crore earlier)

90.s: Which Article provides for the Contingency Fund of a State?
90.x: State Contingency Fund – Established by the State Legislature by law (Art. 267(2)); at the disposal of the Governor, who operates it

90.s: What kind of expenditure is charged expenditure on the CFI with respect to Parliament's vote?
o: Votable only in the Rajya Sabha
90.x: Charged expenditure = expenditure from the CFI that the Constitution makes non-votable – not submitted to the vote of Parliament but can be discussed in either House (Art. 113(1)); it still needs an Appropriation Act (Art. 114).

90.s: Under which Article are the President's emoluments charged on the CFI?
90.x: President – Emoluments, allowances, office expenses (Art. 59(3))

90.s: Under which Article are the salaries of the Speaker and the RS Chairman's deputy charged on the CFI?
90.x: Chairman and Deputy Chairman (RS); Speaker and Deputy Speaker (LS) – Salaries and allowances (Art. 97)

90.s: Under which Article are the salaries of Supreme Court judges charged on the CFI?
90.x: Supreme Court judges – Salaries, allowances, pensions (Art. 125); SC administrative expenses

90.s: What expenditure of High Court judges is charged on the Consolidated Fund of India?
90.x: High Court judges – Only pensions (Art. 112(3)(d)(iii)); salaries charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State (Art. 202(3)(d); fixed under Art. 221)

90.s: Under which Article are the salary and pension of the CAG charged on the CFI?
90.x: CAG – Salary, allowances, pension and office expenses (Art. 148)

90.s: On which fund are a State PSC's expenses charged?
90.x: UPSC chairman and members – Salaries, allowances, pensions (Art. 322); a State PSC's expenses – Consolidated Fund of the State (Art. 322)

90.s: Which sums for court rulings are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India?
o: Sums to satisfy a judgment, decree or award
90.x: Others – Debt charges of the Government of India; sums to satisfy a judgment, decree or arbitral award; anything Parliament declares charged

90.s: Under which Article does Parliament fix Ministers' salaries, which are voted, not charged?
90.x: Prime Minister and Ministers – Salaries fixed by Parliament (Art. 75(6)); voted

90.s: How are the salaries and expenses of the Election Commission treated in the Union Budget?
90.x: Election Commission – Salaries and expenses voted

90.s: In what capacity does the Vice-President draw a salary charged on the CFI?
o: As Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
90.x: Vice-President – No salary as VP; draws it as Chairman of the Rajya Sabha – charged on the CFI

90.s: Under which Article are a Governor's emoluments shared when he serves two or more States?
90.x: Governor – Emoluments charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State (Art. 158(3)); one Governor for two or more States → shared in the proportion the President fixes (Art. 158(3A)); Governors' pensions are outside Art. 112(3)

90.s: Which Schedule contains emoluments, allowances and privileges of constitutional functionaries?
90.x: Second Schedule – emoluments, allowances and privileges; Third Schedule – forms of oaths.

90.s: At which Budget stage is there no discussion on the day itself?
90.x: 1. Presentation – No discussion that day

90.s: How many days does the general discussion on the Budget last in both Houses?
90.x: 2. General discussion – Both Houses, 3-4 days; no cut motion, no vote

90.s: By which committees are demands for grants scrutinised in the third stage of the Budget?
90.x: 3. Scrutiny by the Departmentally Related Standing Committees – House adjourned 3-4 weeks

90.s: Which House votes on the Demands for Grants?
90.x: 4. Voting on Demands for Grants (Art. 113) – Lok Sabha only; it may pass, reject or reduce, never increase; a demand becomes a grant after it is voted

90.s: Under which Article is the Appropriation Bill passed?
90.x: 5. Passing of the Appropriation Bill – Art. 114

90.s: Which is the last stage of the Budget, giving effect to the tax proposals?
90.x: 6. Passing of the Finance Bill – Last stage; gives effect to the tax proposals

90.s: Which is passed after the general discussion but before demands are voted?
90.x: Sequence: Presentation → DRSC scrutiny → Appropriation Bill → Finance Bill; the vote on account is passed after the general discussion (before the demands are voted). Vote on account, vote of credit and exceptional grants are outside the stages of normal financial legislation.

90.s: What is it called when the Speaker puts all remaining demands to vote at once on the last allotted day?
90.x: Guillotine: on the last allotted day the Speaker puts all remaining demands – those not discussed for want of time – to vote at once.

90.s: To what amount does a policy cut reduce a demand?
90.x: Policy cut – To Re 1 – Disapproval of the policy behind the demand

90.s: Which cut motion reduces a demand by a specified amount for economy in expenditure?
90.x: Economy cut – By a specified amount – Economy in expenditure

90.s: How much does a token cut reduce a demand by?
90.x: Token cut – By Rs 100 – Air a specific grievance within the Government's responsibility

90.s: What is the purpose of a token cut?
90.x: Token cut – By Rs 100 – Air a specific grievance within the Government's responsibility

90.s: What does a cut motion propose in a demand for grant?
90.x: Object – Move a proposal to reduce expenditure in a demand for grant and draw the House's attention to a matter

90.s: In which House can cut motions be moved?
90.x: Where – Only in the Lok Sabha, at the voting on Demands for Grants; admitted at the discretion of the Speaker; cannot relate to charged expenditure

90.s: What does the passage of a cut motion signify for the Government?
90.x: Passage – Loss of confidence → the Government is expected to resign

90.s: Under which Article can no money be withdrawn from the CFI except under the Appropriation Act?
90.x: Appropriation Bill – Authorises withdrawal from the CFI for voted grants + charged expenditure; passed by both Houses (as a Money Bill); Art. 114(3): no withdrawal except under it – charged expenditure included

90.s: Which amendments are not allowed in an Appropriation Bill?
o: Varying the amount of a voted grant
90.x: Amendments – No amendment may vary the amount or alter the destination of a voted grant, or vary charged expenditure

90.s: Since when have Appropriation Acts carried an automatic repeal (sunset) clause?
90.x: Automatic repeal clause – Since the Appropriation Act, 2016 (after the Appropriation Acts (Repeal) Act, 2016 repealed 758 old Acts) – an automatic repeal (sunset) clause

90.s: How many days does the government have to enact a Finance Bill?
90.x: Finance Bill – Gives effect to the tax proposals; amendments to reduce or abolish a tax can be moved, not to increase it; enacted within 75 days (Provisional Collection of Taxes Act, 1931)

90.s: Which Article requires a law for changes in existing tax rates?
90.x: Tax rates – Changes in existing rates need law (Art. 265) – usually via the Finance Bill

90.s: Under which Article is a Bill on custody of the CFI and appropriation out of it a Money Bill?
90.x: Money Bill (Art. 110(1)) – Covers custody of the CFI/Contingency Fund and appropriation out of the CFI

90.s: Which of these does India NOT have?
90.x: Placing the AFS; withdrawal only after the Appropriation Act; supplementary grants and vote on account; the Finance Bill. India has no Parliamentary Budget Office.

90.s: Which department of the Finance Ministry prepares the Union Budget?
90.x: The Department of Economic Affairs prepares the Budget; Public Account disbursements need no authorisation by Parliament.

90.s: Which grant is given when the sanctioned amount proves insufficient for the year?
90.x: Supplementary – 115 – Sanctioned amount insufficient for the year

90.s: Which grant is given for a new service not in the Budget?
90.x: Additional – 115 – New service not in the Budget

90.s: Whose approval must come first before an excess grant is voted?
90.x: Excess – 115 – Spent more than granted; voted after the year, PAC approval first

90.s: Under which Article is a vote on account made?
90.x: Vote on account – 116 – Advance grant for part of the year pending passage of the Budget (≈2 months, one-sixth; 3-5 months in election years)

90.s: Which grant is an advance for part of the year pending passage of the Budget?
90.x: Vote on account – 116 – Advance grant for part of the year pending passage of the Budget (≈2 months, one-sixth; 3-5 months in election years)

90.s: Which grant is a blank cheque for an unexpected or indefinite demand?
90.x: Vote of credit – 116 – Blank cheque for an unexpected/indefinite demand

90.s: Which grant is made for a purpose outside the current service of any year?
90.x: Exceptional – 116 – Outside the current service of any year

90.s: How is a new service met under a token grant?
90.x: Token grant – New service met by re-appropriation; token sum voted by the LS

90.s: What does a vote on account let the Government do before the Appropriation Act?
90.x: Vote on account – Needed when the regular Budget will not be passed in time (e.g. an election year); lets the Government withdraw money from the CFI before the Appropriation Act

90.s: When is a vote on account normally needed since the 1 February Budget of 2017?
90.x: Since the 1 February Budget (2017) – Normally needed only in election years (with an Interim Budget) – still in use

90.s: In which year was the February AP Budget a vote-on-account budget, being an election year?
90.x: Andhra Pradesh – The February 2019 AP Budget (election year) was a vote-on-account budget

90.s: Under which Article did the Lok Sabha approve the second batch of Supplementary Demands for Grants 2025-26?
90.x: Latest – The LS approved the second batch of Supplementary Demands for Grants 2025-26 (Art. 115)

91.s: How many members does the Estimates Committee have?
91.x: Estimates – 30 (largest) – None – all 30 from the Lok Sabha – Appointed by the Speaker; invariably from the ruling party

91.s: From which party is the Estimates Committee chairman invariably appointed?
91.x: Estimates – 30 (largest) – None – all 30 from the Lok Sabha – Appointed by the Speaker; invariably from the ruling party

91.s: What is the composition of the Public Accounts Committee?
91.x: Public Accounts (PAC) – 22 = 15 LS + 7 RS – Yes – 7 – Appointed by the Speaker; Opposition member since 1967 (convention)

91.s: How many Rajya Sabha members sit on the Public Accounts Committee?
91.x: Public Accounts (PAC) – 22 = 15 LS + 7 RS – Yes – 7 – Appointed by the Speaker; Opposition member since 1967 (convention)

91.s: Whose member, by the 1967 convention, chairs the PAC?
91.x: Public Accounts (PAC) – 22 = 15 LS + 7 RS – Yes – 7 – Appointed by the Speaker; Opposition member since 1967 (convention)

91.s: What is the composition of the Committee on Public Undertakings?
91.x: Public Undertakings (COPU) – 22 = 15 LS + 7 RS – Yes – 7 – Appointed by the Speaker from its LS members

91.s: Which members does the Speaker choose the COPU chairman from?
91.x: Public Undertakings (COPU) – 22 = 15 LS + 7 RS – Yes – 7 – Appointed by the Speaker from its LS members

91.s: Which are the three financial committees of Parliament?
91.x: The three financial committees – PAC, Estimates, COPU (Business Advisory, Petitions, Government Assurances and Library committees are of other kinds)

91.s: Which committee has no Rajya Sabha member?
91.x: Only committee with no RS member – The Estimates Committee (PAC, COPU, Government Assurances, Petitions have RS members/counterparts)

91.s: How often are members of the financial committees elected by proportional representation?
91.x: Election – Elected every year by proportional representation – single transferable vote; term one year; Ministers ineligible

91.s: What kind of committee is the Public Accounts Committee in terms of the Houses?
91.x: PAC – A joint committee of both Houses (LS members elected by the LS, 7 RS members associated)

91.s: What is the composition of the Committee on Empowerment of Women?
91.x: 20 LS + 10 RS – The SC/ST Welfare and Empowerment of Women committees (the latter joint, 20 LS + 10 RS)

91.s: At which stage do financial committees exercise scrutiny over expenditure?
91.x: Budget = control before spending; financial committees = scrutiny after – they support the budgetary process.

91.s: Under which Act was the Public Accounts Committee first set up in 1921?
91.x: Oldest parliamentary committee – First set up in 1921 under the Government of India Act, 1919; a committee of Parliament under the Speaker from 1950

91.s: Which accounts, besides the CAG's audit reports, does the PAC examine?
91.x: Function – Examines the Appropriation Accounts, Finance Accounts and the CAG's audit reports; checks money was spent "within the scope of the demand"; looks at waste, loss and nugatory expenditure

91.s: Who is described as the "guide, friend and philosopher" of the PAC?
91.x: "Watchdog" – On departmental expenditure and irregularities; the CAG is its "guide, friend and philosopher" and assists it

91.s: What kind of check on expenditure does the PAC exercise?
91.x: Limits – A post-mortem check; not concerned with policy; recommendations advisory; cannot appoint officials or issue orders

91.s: To whom does the Public Accounts Committee submit its reports?
91.x: Reports – To the Speaker / Lok Sabha (a copy laid in the RS)

91.s: Who chaired the Public Accounts Committee during 2009-14?
91.x: 2009-14 (incl. 2010-11) – Murli Manohar Joshi (BJP, Opposition)

91.s: Who is the PAC chairman for 2024-27?
91.x: 2024-27 (as of 2026) – K.C. Venugopal (Congress, Opposition)

91.s: How many Departmentally Related Standing Committees are there?
91.x: Departmental – 24 DRSCs

91.s: Which standing committees belong to the group 'to inquire'?
91.x: To inquire – Petitions, Privileges, Ethics

91.s: Which committee on a social group falls among the committees 'to scrutinise and control'?
91.x: To scrutinise and control – Government Assurances, Subordinate Legislation, Papers Laid, Welfare of SCs and STs, Empowerment of Women, Offices of Profit

91.s: To which group of standing committees do the Business Advisory and Private Members' Bills committees belong?
91.x: Day-to-day business – Business Advisory, Private Members' Bills, Rules, Absence of Members

91.s: To which group of committees do the Library Committee and Salaries of MPs committee belong?
91.x: House-keeping – General Purposes, House, Library, Salaries of MPs

91.s: Which parliamentary committee is called the "Ombudsman" of Parliament?
91.x: Petitions – Petitions on Bills and public-interest matters; representations of citizens – the "Ombudsman" of Parliament – LS 15, RS 10

91.s: What is the strength of the Petitions Committee in each House?
91.x: Petitions – Petitions on Bills and public-interest matters; representations of citizens – the "Ombudsman" of Parliament – LS 15, RS 10

91.s: Which committee checks whether rules and bye-laws under delegated powers are properly exercised by the Executive?
91.x: Subordinate Legislation – Whether rules, regulations, sub-rules, bye-laws made under powers delegated by Parliament or conferred by the Constitution are properly exercised by the Executive – 15 each House (1953)

91.s: In which year was the Committee on Subordinate Legislation set up with 15 members in each House?
91.x: Subordinate Legislation – Whether rules, regulations, sub-rules, bye-laws made under powers delegated by Parliament or conferred by the Constitution are properly exercised by the Executive – 15 each House (1953)

91.s: Which committee tracks ministers' assurances till they are implemented?
91.x: Government Assurances – Tracks ministers' assurances till implemented – LS 15, RS 10 (1953)

91.s: Which committee decides which offices should disqualify MPs?
o: Joint Committee on Offices of Profit
91.x: Joint Committee on Offices of Profit – Which offices should disqualify MPs – 15 = 10 LS + 5 RS

91.s: Which committee examines cases of breach of privilege?
91.x: Privileges – Breach of privilege – LS 15, RS 10

91.s: What does the Ethics Committee of Parliament oversee?
91.x: Ethics – Members' conduct – RS 4 Mar 1997, LS 16 May 2000

91.s: When was the Rajya Sabha Ethics Committee constituted?
91.x: Ethics – Members' conduct – RS 4 Mar 1997, LS 16 May 2000

91.s: Who chairs the Business Advisory Committee of the Lok Sabha?
91.x: Business Advisory – Allots time for Government and other business – LS 15, Speaker chairs

91.s: Whose reports does the Committee on Welfare of SCs and STs examine?
o: National Commissions for SCs and STs
91.x: Welfare of SCs and STs – Reports of the National Commissions for SCs and STs; welfare programmes – 30 = 20 LS + 10 RS; Ministers cannot serve; outside the financial committees

91.s: When was the Committee on Empowerment of Women set up?
91.x: Committee on Empowerment of Women – Both Houses, set up 29 April 1997 – 30 = 20 LS + 10 RS

91.s: What is the strength of the Committee on Empowerment of Women?
91.x: Committee on Empowerment of Women – Both Houses, set up 29 April 1997 – 30 = 20 LS + 10 RS

91.s: Which committee checks that papers laid by Ministers (other than statutory orders) comply with the Constitution or the Act?
o: Committee on Papers Laid on the Table
91.x: Committee on Papers Laid on the Table – Papers laid by Ministers (other than statutory orders, which go to Subordinate Legislation) comply with the Constitution, the Act or rule

91.s: Which committee watches rule-making power delegated to the executive?
o: Committee on Papers Laid on the Table
91.x: Delegated legislation – Rule-making power delegated by the legislature to the executive; watched by the Committee on Subordinate Legislation

91.s: Which committee is found only in the Lok Sabha?
91.x: Lok Sabha-only – Committee on Private Members' Bills and Resolutions; Committee on Absence of Members

91.s: To which group do Subordinate Legislation, Government Assurances and the financial committees belong?
91.x: Watchdog group – Subordinate Legislation, Government Assurances, Estimates, PAC, COPU, DRSCs

91.s: Which committee does the Speaker chair ex officio?
91.x: Speaker as ex-officio chairperson – Business Advisory Committee, Rules Committee, General Purposes Committee (he appoints the chairs of PAC, Estimates, COPU)

91.s: When was the Lok Sabha Ethics Committee first set up ad hoc?

95.s: Which Amendment added the elected MLAs of Delhi and Puducherry to the presidential electoral college?
95.x: Elected members of the Assemblies of NCT Delhi and Puducherry (added by the 70th Amendment, 1992) – Governors, Lt. Governors; UTs without Assemblies (e.g. Chandigarh, Daman and Diu)

95.s: Which Article lays down the manner of election of the President?
95.x: Articles – Art. 54 = electoral college; Art. 55 = manner of election – together the election of the President

95.s: Which UT's elected MLAs take part in electing the President?
95.x: Only "elected" members – Elected MPs + elected MLAs (States, Delhi, Puducherry); nominated MPs are out

95.s: What kind of election chooses the President through elected representatives?
95.x: Indirect election – Chosen by the elected representatives – not directly by the people, nor by Parliament alone

95.s: From which country is the presidential election by PR-STV borrowed?
95.x: Art. 55(3) – Proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote, by secret ballot – borrowed from Ireland

95.s: Besides the President, which other members are elected by PR-STV?
95.x: PR-STV also for – Vice-President, Rajya Sabha members, Legislative Council members; Lok Sabha and State Assembly members are elected directly (first-past-the-post)

95.s: How is the value of an MLA's vote in the presidential election calculated?
95.x: MLA – Population of the State ÷ elected MLAs × 1/1000 – Varies from State to State (uniformity among States, Art. 55(1))

95.s: Under which Article must there be uniformity among States in the scale of MLA vote values?
95.x: MLA – Population of the State ÷ elected MLAs × 1/1000 – Varies from State to State (uniformity among States, Art. 55(1))

95.s: How does the value of an MP's vote vary across Houses in the presidential election?
95.x: MP – Total value of all MLAs' votes ÷ total elected MPs – Same for every MP, Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha (parity between the Union and the States)

95.s: Which Census is the population base for presidential vote values?
95.x: Population base: 1971 Census – frozen by the 42nd Amendment (till 2000) and then by the 84th Amendment (2001) till the first Census after 2026.

95.s: What was the 2022 vote value of a Kerala MLA?
95.x: Vote value depends on the population–seats ratio, not on the number of seats: Puducherry MLA 16 > Arunachal Pradesh MLA 8; Kerala MLA 152 > Madhya Pradesh MLA 131 (2022 values).

95.s: How many proposers and seconders were needed for a presidential candidate from 1974 to 1997?
95.x: Nomination – At least 50 electors as proposers and 50 as seconders (since 1997; 10 + 10 from 1974 to 1997); deposit ₹15,000; Vice-President: 20 + 20

95.s: On which preference votes did V.V. Giri win the 1969 election?
95.x: Quota – More than half of valid vote value; lowest candidate eliminated and votes transferred (V.V. Giri, 1969, won on second-preference votes)

95.s: Which body alone decides disputes over a presidential election under Art. 71?
95.x: Art. 71 – Disputes decided only by the Supreme Court, whose decision is final; acts done before the election is declared void remain valid ("not invalidated")

95.s: Why do members of a dissolved Assembly not vote in a presidential election?
95.x: Art. 71(4) – Election cannot be challenged or postponed because of vacancies in the electoral college – members of a dissolved Assembly simply do not vote

95.s: Which Act governs presidential and vice-presidential elections, including the Returning Officer?
95.x: Returning Officer – The Election Commission appoints the Secretary-General of the Lok Sabha or of the Rajya Sabha, by rotation (Presidential and Vice-Presidential Elections Act, 1952)

95.s: Who take part in impeaching the President but not in electing him?
95.x: Elected MLAs vote in the election but take no part in impeachment (Parliament alone impeaches); nominated MPs do the reverse; Legislative Councils do neither.

95.s: Which body is part of the presidential electoral college but not of impeachment?
95.x: Part of the electoral college but not of impeachment = State Legislative Assemblies.

95.s: Who form the electoral college of the Vice-President?
95.x: Electoral colleges compared: President = elected MPs + elected MLAs; Vice-President = all MPs; Rajya Sabha = elected MLAs; Lok Sabha = the people – a Lok Sabha member shares no electoral college with the others.

95.s: To whom does the President address his resignation?
95.x: Term: 5 years from the date he enters upon his office; resignation in writing to the Vice-President; continues until the successor enters office

95.s: How many times can a person be re-elected President?
95.x: Eligibility for re-election – any number of times, no upper limit

95.s: Besides age 35, for election to which House must a presidential candidate be qualified?
95.x: Qualifications: citizen of India; 35 years completed; qualified for election to the Lok Sabha; no office of profit

95.s: Which accommodation is the President entitled to use without paying rent?
95.x: Conditions of office: not a member of any legislature; no office of profit; rent-free residence; emoluments cannot be diminished

95.s: Who administers the oath of office to the President?
95.x: Oath before the CJI (in his absence the senior-most SC judge)

95.s: Which kind of citizenship does a presidential candidate need under Art. 58?
95.x: Art. 58 – outside the requirements – Education, citizenship by birth (any citizen), a maximum age (none); qualified for the Lok Sabha (House of the People)

95.s: Who among these does not hold an office of profit for presidential eligibility?
95.x: Office of profit – Holder of an office of profit under the Union, a State or a local authority is not eligible; the offices of President, VP, Governor and Union/State Minister are not offices of profit

95.s: What happens to an MP's seat when he becomes President?
95.x: Art. 59 – An MP or MLA may contest; his seat is deemed vacated on the date he enters upon his office as President

95.s: To whom does the Vice-President communicate the President's resignation?
95.x: Resignation – Addressed to the Vice-President, who communicates it to the Speaker of the Lok Sabha

95.s: Who administers the oath to the President under Art. 60?
95.x: Oath (Art. 60) – To faithfully execute the office, preserve, protect and defend the Constitution and the law, and devote himself to the service and well-being of the people of India – administered by the CJI

95.s: What is the President's salary under the Finance Act, 2018?
95.x: Emoluments – Fixed by Parliament by law (originally the Second Schedule); charged on the Consolidated Fund; cannot be diminished during the term; salary ₹5 lakh per month (Finance Act, 2018, w.e.f. 1 January 2016)

95.s: Who holds office if the successor has not entered office when the President's five years end?
95.x: Term continues – If the successor has not entered office when the 5 years end, the outgoing President continues

95.s: Which Article lays down the procedure for removal of the President?
95.x: Art. 61 – Procedure for impeachment (removal) of the President; Art. 56(1)(b) refers to it

95.s: What is the only ground for impeaching the President?
95.x: Only ground – "Violation of the Constitution" – the term is undefined in the Constitution

95.s: Who removes the President from office?
95.x: Who removes him – Parliament (the two Houses)

95.s: In which House can the impeachment of the President be initiated?
95.x: Initiated – In either House of Parliament (Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha)

95.s: What is the nature of the procedure of impeachment of the President?
95.x: Nature – Quasi-judicial procedure; borrowed from the USA; no President has ever been impeached

95.s: How many days' written notice is needed for an impeachment resolution against the President?
95.x: Notice – 14 days' written notice, resolution signed by one-fourth of the total members of the initiating House

95.s: What majority must the initiating House pass the impeachment charge by?
95.x: Initiating House – Passes the charge by two-thirds of its total membership

95.s: What does the other House do with the impeachment charge before voting?
o: Refers it to the Supreme Court
95.x: Other House – Investigates the charge (President may appear or be represented) and sustains it by two-thirds of its total membership → removed from that date

95.s: Who take part in impeachment of the President, unlike in his election?
95.x: Nominated MPs take part; elected MLAs (States, Delhi, Puducherry) do not – removal by the national Parliament alone keeps it free from narrow regional considerations.

95.s: For whom alone is the term "impeachment" used in the Constitution?
95.x: "Impeachment" is used only for the President; judges and the Vice-President are "removed". VP removal: Rajya Sabha resolution by a majority of all its then members, agreed to by the Lok Sabha; no ground is specified.

95.s: Where must a resolution to remove the Vice-President be passed first?
95.x: "Impeachment" is used only for the President; judges and the Vice-President are "removed". VP removal: Rajya Sabha resolution by a majority of all its then members, agreed to by the Lok Sabha; no ground is specified.

95.s: Under which Article is the executive power of the Union vested in the President?
95.x: Art. 53 – The executive power of the Union is vested in the President, exercised directly or through subordinate officers in accordance with the Constitution – limited (Art. 74: aid and advice)

95.s: What does Art. 53(2) vest in the President?
o: Power to dissolve the Lok Sabha
Supreme Command of the Defence Forces
95.x: Art. 53(2) – Supreme Command of the Defence Forces vested in the President (regulated by law)

95.s: Under which Part and Chapter of the Constitution is the Union executive dealt with?
95.x: Union executive – President, Vice-President, Prime Minister, Council of Ministers and Attorney General (Part V, Chapter I)

95.s: Under which Article does the President make regulations for UTs like Lakshadweep?
95.x: Executive – Appoints the PM and on his advice other Ministers; Governors (Art. 155), CAG (Art. 148), AG (Art. 76), Election Commissioners (Art. 324), UPSC, Finance Commission; Ambassadors and High Commissioners; administers UTs; Art. 240 regulations for A&N, Lakshadweep, DNH and Daman & Diu, and Puducherry when its Assembly is suspended or dissolved

95.s: Under which Article does the President dissolve the Lok Sabha?
95.x: Legislative – Integral part of Parliament (Art. 79: President + Lok Sabha + Rajya Sabha); summons and prorogues the Houses, dissolves the Lok Sabha (Art. 85); summons a joint sitting (Art. 108 – presided over by the Speaker); addresses and sends messages (Art. 86); special address (Art. 87); nominates 12 to the Rajya Sabha; assent to Bills; ordinances

95.s: Which Bills can be introduced only on the President's recommendation?
95.x: Financial – Budget laid in his name; Money Bills and demands for grants only on his recommendation; advances from the Contingency Fund; constitutes the Finance Commission

95.s: Under which Article does the President seek the Supreme Court's advisory opinion?
95.x: Judicial – Appoints SC/HC judges (Third Judges Case 1998: CJI + four senior-most judges collegium); Art. 143 advisory opinion – not binding; Art. 72 pardon

95.s: On which body's advice does the President declare war and conclude peace?
95.x: Diplomatic and military – Treaties in his name; sends and receives envoys; declares war and concludes peace on the Council's advice

95.s: Under which Article does the President proclaim a Financial Emergency?
95.x: Emergency – Art. 352 National, Art. 356 President's Rule, Art. 360 Financial

95.s: Under which Article does a Money Bill need the President's prior recommendation?
95.x: Prior recommendation of the President – Money Bills (Art. 117), Art. 3 Bills (new States, boundaries), Bills involving expenditure from the Consolidated Fund, State Bills restricting trade (Art. 304); Constitution Amendment Bills need none

95.s: Under which Article are the CAG's reports laid before Parliament by the President?
95.x: Reports laid before Parliament by the President – Finance Commission (Art. 281), CAG (Art. 151), National Commission for SCs (Art. 338), UPSC, Linguistic Minorities – the PAC report goes from Parliament's own committee

95.s: Which Article makes it the PM's duty to communicate Cabinet decisions to the President?
95.x: Art. 78 (PM's duties) – Communicate all decisions of the Council of Ministers on administration and proposals for legislation; furnish information the President calls for; place before the Council a matter decided by a single Minister if the President so requires

95.s: Under which Article does the President make a special address at the first session of each year?
95.x: Address to Parliament (Art. 87) – First session after each general election and first session of each year; speech prepared by the Union Cabinet; with Art. 86 (address and messages)

95.s: Whose advice does the President act on when the Lok Sabha is dissolved?
95.x: When the Lok Sabha is dissolved – The Council of Ministers continues (Art. 75 needs one at all times); the President still acts on its advice

95.s: Who is described as the first citizen of India, who "represents the nation but does not lead" it?
95.x: First citizen of India – "Represents the nation but does not lead the nation" (the PM leads)

95.s: When did President Pratibha Patil address both Houses at the start of the Budget Session?
95.x: 12 March 2012 – President Pratibha Patil addressed both Houses together at the start of the Budget Session

95.s: Which of these is a cause of vacancy in the office of President?
95.x: Causes of vacancy – Expiry of term, death, resignation, removal by impeachment, disqualification, election declared void

95.s: Who holds office if the election of a new President is delayed beyond the term's expiry?
95.x: Art. 62(1) – expiry – Election completed before the term expires; if delayed, the outgoing President continues (no vacancy)

95.s: Within which period must a vacancy in the President's office by death be filled?
95.x: Art. 62(2) – death, resignation, removal or otherwise – Election within six months; the new President gets a full five-year term

95.s: Who acts as President when the office falls vacant by death, resignation or removal?
95.x: Art. 65(1) – Vacancy by death, resignation or removal → the Vice-President acts as President until the new President enters office

95.s: Under which clause does the VP discharge the President's functions when he is ill or absent?
95.x: Art. 65(2) – The VP discharges the functions when the President is absent, ill or otherwise unable

95.s: What powers and emoluments does the VP enjoy while acting as President?
o: All powers, immunities and emoluments of the President
The Chairman's salary plus the President's powers
95.x: While acting – The VP has all the powers, immunities and emoluments of the President; the Deputy Chairman presides over the Rajya Sabha

95.s: Who acts as President when both the President's and Vice-President's offices are vacant?
95.x: Both offices vacant – The Chief Justice of India, or in his absence the senior-most SC judge – President (Discharge of Functions) Act, 1969

95.s: When did V.V. Giri act as President after Zakir Husain's death?
95.x: V.V. Giri (VP) – 3 May – 20 July 1969 – Zakir Husain died in office

95.s: Whose death in office made V.V. Giri acting President in 1969?
95.x: V.V. Giri (VP) – 3 May – 20 July 1969 – Zakir Husain died in office

95.s: When did CJI M. Hidayatullah act as President?
95.x: M. Hidayatullah (CJI) – 20 July – 24 August 1969 – Giri resigned as VP to contest; both offices vacant

95.s: Why did the CJI act as President in 1969?
95.x: M. Hidayatullah (CJI) – 20 July – 24 August 1969 – Giri resigned as VP to contest; both offices vacant

95.s: When did B.D. Jatti act as President?
95.x: B.D. Jatti (VP) – February – July 1977 – Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed died in office

95.s: Whose death in office made B.D. Jatti acting President in 1977?
95.x: B.D. Jatti (VP) – February – July 1977 – Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed died in office

95.s: When did Vice-President M. Hidayatullah discharge the President's functions?
95.x: M. Hidayatullah (VP) – 6–31 October 1982 – Discharged the functions while Zail Singh was abroad for surgery

95.s: Why did VP M. Hidayatullah discharge the President's functions in 1982?
o: Zail Singh was abroad for surgery
95.x: M. Hidayatullah (VP) – 6–31 October 1982 – Discharged the functions while Zail Singh was abroad for surgery

95.s: Who is the only person to have been CJI, acting President and Vice-President?
95.x: M. Hidayatullah – the only CJI to act as President (1969); the only person who has been CJI, acting President and Vice-President (1979–84); he performed the President's functions twice (1969 as CJI, 1982 as VP). Other CJIs such as P.N. Bhagwati and P.B. Gajendragadkar never acted.

95.s: What kind of executive is the President of India?
95.x: Position – Nominal / de jure executive and constitutional head of the State; the PM and Council of Ministers are the real / de facto executive

95.s: Why is the executive power of the Union vested in the President?
o: The constitutional Head of the State
95.x: Executive power – Vested in the President because he is the constitutional Head of the State

95.s: Under which Article does a Council of Ministers headed by the PM aid and advise the President?
95.x: Art. 74(1) – Council of Ministers headed by the PM to aid and advise the President

95.s: Which Amendment made the Council's advice binding on the President?
95.x: 42nd Amendment (1976) – Advice made binding ("shall act")

95.s: Which Amendment lets the President return the Council's advice once for reconsideration?
95.x: 44th Amendment (1978) – He may return the advice once for reconsideration, then must act on it – his influence on ministers

95.s: Under which clause can courts not inquire into what advice Ministers gave the President?
95.x: Art. 74(2) – Whether and what advice was tendered cannot be inquired into by any court

95.s: Which Article makes the President not answerable to any court for official acts?
95.x: Art. 361 – President/Governor not answerable to any court for official acts; no criminal proceedings during the term; civil proceedings only after two months' written notice; no court can compel a Governor to perform a duty

95.s: Who is called the "keystone of the Cabinet arch"?
95.x: PM – "Keystone of the Cabinet arch" – the President is only the formal head

95.s: Which of these does the President do without discretion, on ministerial advice (unlike appointing a PM in a hung House)?
o: PM's duty to keep the President informed
Reports laid before Parliament by the President
95.x: Appointing a PM when no party has a clear majority – Summoning and proroguing Parliament

95.s: Which of these does the President do without discretion, on the Council of Ministers' advice?
o: Appointing a PM when no party has a majority
Dismissing a Ministry that has lost confidence
95.x: Dismissing a Ministry that has lost confidence – Appointing Ministers

95.s: Which is a situational discretion of the President?
o: Dissolving the Lok Sabha when the Ministry has lost its majority
Summoning Parliament on the PM's advice
Appointing the majority leader as PM
95.x: Dissolving the Lok Sabha if the Ministry lost its majority – Appointing the majority leader as PM (a convention)

95.s: Which of these does the President do without discretion, on the Council of Ministers' advice?
o: Dismissing a Ministry that has lost confidence
95.x: Day-to-day decisions under a caretaker government – Assent to Bills

95.s: Which veto lets the President keep a Bill pending indefinitely?
95.x: Suspensive veto (returning a Bill), pocket veto (keeping a Bill pending); asking the Council to reconsider advice

95.s: What kind of discretion does the President have?
95.x: The President has situational discretion only – no constitutional discretion.

95.s: Which Articles form Part V, Chapter I on the Union Executive?
95.x: Arts. 52–78 = Part V, Chapter I – the Union Executive (Chapter II = Parliament; Part VI = the States).

95.s: Which Article vests the executive power of the Union in the President?
95.x: 52 / 53 – There shall be a President / executive power of the Union vested in him

95.x: 54 / 55 – Election (electoral college) / manner of election

95.s: Which Article lays down the qualifications for election as President?
95.x: 56 / 57 / 58 – Term / re-election / qualifications

95.s: Which Article provides for impeachment of the President?
95.x: 59 / 60 / 61 / 62 – Conditions of office / oath / impeachment / time of election to fill vacancy

95.s: Which Article says 'There shall be a Vice-President of India'?
95.x: 63 / 64 – There shall be a Vice-President / VP ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha

95.s: Which Article provides for the Vice-President to act as President?
95.x: 65 – Vice-President to act as President

95.s: Which Article deals with the election of the Vice-President?
95.x: 66 / 67 / 68 – Election of VP / term and removal of VP / time of election to fill VP vacancy

95.s: Which Article deals with disputes over the election of the President?
95.x: 71 – Election disputes (Supreme Court)

95.s: Which Article gives the President the power of pardon?
95.x: 72 – Pardon

95.s: Which Amendment capped the Council of Ministers at 15% of the Lok Sabha?
95.x: 74 / 75 – Council of Ministers to aid and advise / other provisions – 75(1A) Council not above 15% of Lok Sabha (91st Amendment, 2003)

95.s: Which Article lays down the PM's duty to keep the President informed?
95.x: 76 / 77 / 78 – Attorney General / conduct of business / PM's duty to keep the President informed

95.s: Who form the electoral college of the President?
95.x: Electors – Elected MPs + elected MLAs – All MPs, elected and nominated (no MLAs)

95.s: For which House must a vice-presidential candidate be qualified for election?
95.x: Qualified for – Lok Sabha – Rajya Sabha

95.s: How many proposers and seconders does a presidential candidate need now?
95.x: Nomination – 50 + 50 – 20 + 20

95.s: How many proposers and seconders does a vice-presidential candidate need?
95.x: Nomination – 50 + 50 – 20 + 20

95.s: Under which Article is the President removed by impeachment?
95.x: Removal – Impeachment (Art. 61) – Rajya Sabha resolution agreed to by the Lok Sabha

95.s: How is the Vice-President removed from office?
o: Rajya Sabha resolution agreed to by the Lok Sabha
95.x: Removal – Impeachment (Art. 61) – Rajya Sabha resolution agreed to by the Lok Sabha

95.s: To whom does the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha address his resignation as VP?
95.x: Resigns to – Vice-President – President

95.s: Which Article sets no six-month deadline for filling a vacancy in the Vice-President's office?

95.s: Which Amendment ended the joint-meeting method for electing the Vice-President?
95.x: 11th Amendment (1961) – Ended the joint-meeting method for electing the VP (now an electoral college of all MPs)

95.s: How many members formed the electoral college in the 2022 VP election?
95.x: 2022 VP election – Electoral college of 788 members

95.s: Which Vice-President resigned in July 2025?

95.s: On which Bills is the President's absolute veto typically used?
o: Bills passed at a joint sitting
95.x: Absolute – Withholds assent – private members' Bills; Government Bills after the Cabinet resigns – Yes

95.s: Which veto lets the President return a Bill once, but he must assent if it is re-passed?

95.s: Why is the pocket veto possible for the Indian President?
95.x: Pocket – Keeps the Bill pending – the Constitution fixes no time limit – Yes

95.s: Which veto, overridable by a higher majority, exists in the USA but not in India?
95.x: Qualified – Overridable by a higher majority (USA) – No

95.s: Which Amendment made assent to a Constitution Amendment Bill obligatory for the President?
95.x: Constitution Amendment Bill: the President must give assent (24th Amendment, 1971). The 2025 Presidential Reference (opinion of 20 November 2025) held that courts cannot fix timelines or create "deemed assent".

95.s: When can the President promulgate an ordinance under Art. 123?
o: When Parliament is not in session
95.x: When – Only when Parliament (either House) is not in session

95.s: When does an ordinance lapse after Parliament reassembles?

95.s: Which case held re-promulgation of ordinances in Bihar a fraud on the Constitution?
95.x: D.C. Wadhwa (1987) – Re-promulgation in Bihar a fraud on the Constitution

95.s: Which form of clemency removes both the sentence and the conviction?
95.x: Pardon – Removes both sentence and conviction

95.s: What is it called when a death sentence is changed to rigorous life imprisonment?

96.s: Which Article empowers the President to grant pardons, reprieves, respites or remissions?

96.s: What does a pardon remove?

96.s: Why is a reprieve, a temporary stay of execution, granted?
o: To allow time to seek a pardon

96.s: What is the changing of a death sentence into life imprisonment called?

96.s: Which sentences, besides those for Union-law offences and death, come under Art. 72?

96.s: What kind of power is the President's pardoning power, strictly speaking?
o: Executive power independent of the judiciary
Power shared with the Supreme Court

96.s: Which 1980 case held that the President exercises the pardoning power on the Council's advice?

96.s: What kind of review applies to the exercise of the pardoning power?
o: Limited judicial review (mala fide, arbitrary grounds)

96.s: What does the President do with a Bill under a pocket veto?
o: Keeps it pending without time limit
Refers it to the Supreme Court

96.s: In which year was the Indian Post Office (Amendment) Bill, the object of a pocket veto, passed?

101.s: Which of these is an individual privilege of members (not a collective privilege of the House)?
o: Exclude strangers and hold secret sittings
Punish members and outsiders for contempt
Freedom of speech in the House and committees

101.s: Which of these is an individual privilege of members (not a collective privilege of the House)?
o: Make its own rules of procedure
Freedom from arrest in civil cases

101.s: Which of these is an individual privilege of members (not a collective privilege of the House)?
o: Exclude strangers and hold secret sittings
101.x: Make its own rules; regulate internal affairs – Exemption from jury service; may refuse to attend as a witness while the House sits

101.s: What kind of privilege is receiving immediate information of a member's arrest?
101.x: Receive immediate information of a member's arrest, detention, conviction or release

101.x: No arrest or legal process within the precincts without the presiding officer's permission

101.s: Which is wider in scope?
o: Freedom of speech in the House

101.s: Who gives the final decision on a Lok Sabha member's defection?

101.s: What time limit does the Tenth Schedule fix for deciding defection cases?
101.x: No time limit – None in the Schedule; Speakers stay members of their parties – hence delays

101.x: Para 7 (bar on courts) – Struck down in Kihoto – it needed State ratification under Art. 368(2)

101.x: Judicial review only after the decision – Limited grounds – mala fides, perversity, natural justice, constitutional mandate

102.s: Which head of state is the Indian President compared to as a de jure head?

102.s: Which clause makes the Council's advice binding on the President?
102.x: Aid and advice – Art. 74(1): advice binding on the President

102.s: Under which clause does the President appoint the Prime Minister?
102.x: Majority party rule – President appoints (Art. 75(1)) the leader of the majority party in the Lok Sabha, or of the alliance with a majority there, as PM – a convention

102.s: Which clause makes ministers "swim and sink together" before the Lok Sabha?
102.x: Collective responsibility – Art. 75(3): to the Lok Sabha only; ministers hold office together while they command a majority – “swim and sink together”

102.s: Which clause makes Union ministers individually responsible to the President?
102.x: Individual responsibility – Art. 75(2): ministers hold office during the pleasure of the President – individually responsible to the President (dismissed on the PM's advice)

102.s: Within which period must a non-member minister enter Parliament under Art. 75(5)?
102.x: Double membership – Ministers are MPs of either House; a non-member must enter Parliament within six months (Art. 75(5)), else ceases to be a minister

102.s: Of which House is the PM, if a member, the Leader?
102.x: Leadership of the PM – Heads the Council of Ministers; Leader of the Lok Sabha (if a member) and chief spokesperson

102.s: Whose advice can lead to the early dissolution of the Lok Sabha?
102.x: Dissolution – Lok Sabha can be dissolved early on the PM's advice

102.s: Which of these is a convention not written in the Constitution?

102.s: Who heads the Union Cabinet?

102.s: Which members can be in the Union Cabinet?
102.x: Cabinet membership – Not restricted to Lok Sabha members

102.s: Which is another name for the parliamentary system?

102.s: What must the executive retain to stay in power in a parliamentary system?
102.x: Essence – The executive stays in power only while it has a majority (confidence) in the popular House

102.s: Under which clause is the Council of Ministers responsible to the Lok Sabha, India's defining test?
102.x: Defining test – India is parliamentary because the Council of Ministers is responsible to the Lok Sabha (Art. 75(3); States Art. 164(2))

102.s: What is an executive dependent on the support of a legislative majority called?
102.x: Parliamentary executive – An executive dependent on the support of a majority in Parliament

102.s: What is the main principle of the parliamentary system?
102.x: Main principle – Responsibility of the executive to the legislature; the legislature controls the executive

102.s: Which device lets Parliament remove the government?
102.x: Removal – The government is responsible to Parliament and can be removed by it (no-confidence)

102.s: Which principle is the parliamentary system based on?
102.x: Basis – Fusion of powers – co-operation of legislature and executive (presidential = separation of powers; independent legislature and executive)

102.s: At which levels does the Constitution set up the parliamentary system?
102.x: Source of authority – The Constitution sets up the parliamentary system at the Centre and in the States; both draw authority from the Constitution

102.s: How are ministers in a parliamentary system typically described?
102.x: India = secular, federal, parliamentary – parliamentary, cabinet and responsible government; ministers are amateurs, not experts.

102.s: What is the President's role in the parliamentary system?
o: Represents the nation but does not rule
102.x: The President represents the nation but does not rule it; the executive is accountable to the legislature.

102.s: Who is both Head of State and Head of Government in the presidential system?
102.x: Executive – President = Head of State and Head of Government – single executive; all executive power vested in him

102.s: How many years is the US President elected for?
102.x: Election and term – Directly elected for a fixed term (US: electoral college, 4 years); removable only by impeachment

102.s: What can the President in a presidential system not do to the legislature?
102.x: Legislature – President is not accountable to it and cannot dissolve it

102.s: To whom are the secretaries of a presidential system responsible?
102.x: Ministers – Appoints his own Council of Ministers (secretaries) – not legislators, responsible only to him

102.s: Which US feature checks the separation of powers through veto and impeachment?
102.x: Principle – Separation of powers with checks and balances – veto, Senate confirmation, impeachment

102.s: Which term describes the division of powers between Centre and States?
102.x: Other terms – Fusion of powers = parliamentary; division of powers = federalism

102.s: Where was the presidential system first formed?
102.x: Origin – First formed in the USA (oldest and purest form); India, Canada and Britain are parliamentary

102.s: What kind of executive does the presidential system have?
102.x: Nominal head + real head (PM) – dual executive – One person is both heads – single executive

102.s: Where are the secretaries of a presidential system drawn from?
102.x: Collective executive (cabinet); ministers are legislators – Secretaries outside the legislature

102.s: Which principle is the presidential system based on?
102.x: Fusion of powers – Separation of powers

102.s: How can the US President be removed before his fixed term?
102.x: Removable by no-confidence – Fixed term; removable only by impeachment

102.s: Who can dissolve the lower House early in a presidential system?
102.x: Lower House can be dissolved early – No dissolution

102.s: In which year did France's semi-presidential Fifth Republic begin?

102.s: Which country has a parliamentary system?
102.x: Parliamentary – UK, Japan, Canada, India

102.s: Where was the parliamentary form first introduced?

102.s: How is India's head of State chosen?

102.x: Supremacy – Constitutional supremacy (written Constitution) – Sovereignty of Parliament

102.x: Ministers – Non-member allowed for six months – Must be MPs

102.s: Which British PM resigned as Conservative leader in July 2022?
102.x: Removal of the PM – Loss of Lok Sabha confidence – Ruling party can replace him (e.g. Boris Johnson, PM 2019-22, resigned as Conservative leader July 2022)

102.s: Which feature is common to India and Britain?

102.x: Executive – Parliamentary – Presidential

102.s: What is the chief merit of the parliamentary system?
102.x: Parliamentary – Responsible government – executive continuously accountable; harmony of legislature and executive; prevents despotism; ready alternative government – Unstable government; no continuity of policy; cabinet dictatorship with a large majority; “government by amateurs”; against separation of powers

102.s: What is a merit of the presidential system?
102.x: Presidential – Stable, fixed-term executive; continuity of policy; experts as secretaries – Executive-legislature deadlock; personality cult; irresponsible executive

102.s: Which Acts gave India the familiarity that led it to choose the parliamentary system?

102.s: What did the Draft Constitution prefer according to Dr B.R. Ambedkar?

102.s: What is rule by the old called?

107.s: What kind of feature is a single Constitution for the Union and the States?
107.x: Written Constitution – Single Constitution for Union and States (only ex-J&K had its own)

107.s: Which unitary feature lets Parliament alone amend most provisions?
107.x: Division of powers (Seventh Schedule) – Flexibility – most provisions amended by Parliament alone; States not indestructible (Art. 3)

107.s: Which Emergency Article is especially cited as a unitary feature?
107.x: Rigid Constitution – federal provisions need ratification by half the States – Emergency provisions (esp. Art. 356)

107.s: Under which Article does India have single citizenship?
107.x: Independent judiciary – Single citizenship (Art. 9); integrated judiciary

107.s: Which unitary feature, besides integrated audit, does India have?
107.x: Bicameralism – Rajya Sabha represents the States – All India Services; integrated audit (CAG); integrated election machinery

107.s: Under which Article does Parliament have authority over the State List?
107.x: Decentralisation – Appointment of Governor by the Centre; veto over State Bills (President's approval); Parliament's authority over the State List (Art. 249)

107.s: Which is the essential federal feature that settles Centre-State disputes?
107.x: Essential federal feature – Independence of the judiciary – interprets the Constitution, settles Centre-State disputes

107.s: Which House signifies the federal structure of India?
107.x: Why India is federal – The distribution of powers between the Union and the States; the Rajya Sabha signifies the federal structure

107.s: Which office, besides the Governor, is cited as non-federal?
107.x: Non-federal – Office of the Governor, CAG; India is not the “result of an agreement among the federating units”

107.s: From which country's model is residuary power with Parliament taken?
107.x: Not violative of federalism – The three-List division and residuary power with Parliament (Canadian model)

107.s: Under which Articles is the Governor appointed by the President?
107.x: Governor – Appointed by the President (Arts 155-156)

107.s: Through which body are the All India Services recruited?
107.x: All India Services (Art. 312) – Recruited through the UPSC, controlled by the Centre

107.s: What does an amendment affecting the federal structure need besides Parliament's special majority?
107.x: Constitutional amendment affecting the federal structure – Ratification by at least half the States (Art. 368(2) proviso)

107.s: How many States have bicameral legislatures in 2026?
107.x: Bicameral State legislatures – Only six States (AP, Telangana, UP, Bihar, Maharashtra, Karnataka) have a Legislative Council

107.s: Which 2017 reform is cited as a uniform, centralising arrangement?
107.x: 'One Nation One Tax' (GST, 2017) – A uniform, centralising arrangement – not a feature of a true federation

107.s: From which country is a federation with a strong Centre borrowed?
107.x: Federation with a strong Centre, residuary powers with the Centre, Governor appointed by the Centre, “Union” – Canada

107.s: From which country is the Concurrent List borrowed?
107.x: Concurrent List – Australia

107.s: From which Act are the federal scheme and Office of Governor borrowed?
107.x: Federal scheme, Office of Governor, emergency provisions, judiciary – GoI Act, 1935

107.s: From which country is suspension of FRs during Emergency borrowed?
107.x: Suspension of FRs during emergency – Weimar (Germany)

107.s: From which country are single citizenship and the parliamentary system borrowed?
107.x: Single citizenship, parliamentary system – UK

107.s: Which of these features is found in Part V of the Constitution?
107.x: Bicameralism (Parliament) – Part V

107.s: In which Part of the Constitution are the Emergency provisions?
107.x: Emergency – Part XVIII

107.s: Which of these features is found in Part IV of the Constitution?
107.x: Welfare State (DPSP) – Part IV

107.s: What kind of feature of the Indian polity is a written Constitution?
107.x: Written Constitution – Single Constitution for Union and States (only ex-J&K had its own)

107.s: Which unitary feature goes with an integrated judiciary?
107.x: Independent judiciary – Single citizenship; integrated judiciary

107.s: Which unitary feature is the Centre's appointment of the State head?
107.x: Appointment of Governor by the Centre; veto over State Bills (President's approval); Parliament's authority over the State List (Art. 249)

107.s: Why is India called federal?
107.x: India is federal because of the distribution of powers between the Union and the States; the Rajya Sabha signifies the federal structure.

107.s: Which feature is consistent with federalism?
107.x: Against federal principles: Governor, CAG, Emergency powers (esp. Art. 356) – the President taking over a State under emergency. Consistent with federalism: the three-List division and residuary power with Parliament (Canadian model).

107.s: Under which Article are the All India Services created?
107.x: All India Services – Art. 312; recruited through the UPSC and controlled by the Centre

107.s: Under which proviso must half the States ratify federal amendments?
107.x: Amendment of the federal structure – Ratification by at least half the States (Art. 368(2) proviso)

107.s: What does the Indian federation's formation by disintegration resemble?
107.x: The Indian federal system is based on the Canadian model (formation by disintegration, the term "Union", centralising tendency), not the American.

107.s: What does Part XVIII of the Constitution deal with?
107.x: Emergency – Part XVIII

107.s: Who called India "quasi-federal"?
107.x: K.C. Wheare – “Quasi-federal” – “a unitary state with subsidiary federal features rather than a federal state with subsidiary unitary features”

107.s: Who called India "a federation with a strong centralising tendency"?
107.x: Ivor Jennings – “A federation with a strong centralising tendency”

107.s: Who described Indian federalism as "cooperative federalism"?
107.x: Granville Austin – “Cooperative federalism”; author of *The Indian Constitution: Cornerstone of a Nation*

107.s: Who described Indian federalism as "bargaining federalism"?
107.x: Morris-Jones – “Bargaining federalism”

107.s: Who called India "extremely federal"?
107.x: Paul Appleby – “Extremely federal”

107.s: Who called Indian federalism "a case sui generis"?
107.x: Alexandrowicz – “A case sui generis”

107.s: Which scholar: Constitution “avoids the tight mould of federalism” and “could be both unitary as well as federal according to…?
107.x: B.R. Ambedkar – Constitution “avoids the tight mould of federalism” and “could be both unitary as well as federal according to the requirements of time and circumstances”

107.s: Which scholar: Unitary bias grew from financial dependence of States and the Planning Commission?
107.x: K. Santhanam – Unitary bias grew from financial dependence of States and the Planning Commission

107.s: Who called the Emergency powers a "fraud on the Constitution"?
107.x: K.M. Nambiar – Emergency powers a “fraud on the Constitution”

107.s: Who called the Constitution "elephantine"?
107.x: H.V. Kamath – “Elephantine” Constitution (the CA's seal was an elephant)

107.s: Who called India "a comprehensive culture of continental scope"?
107.x: Carl Friedrich – India “not a nation in the traditional western sense but a comprehensive culture of continental scope”

107.s: Which Indian scholar called India "quasi-federal", a combination of both?
107.x: D.D. Basu – Neither purely federal nor purely unitary but a combination of both – “quasi-federal”

107.s: Who described India as "fundamentally federal with pronounced unitary elements"?
107.x: Supreme Court – “Fundamentally federal with pronounced unitary elements”

107.s: What is India called because its unitary features tilt power to the Centre?
107.x: Standard label: “federal system with unitary bias” / “federal in form, unitary in spirit” – the reverse of Wheare's “unitary with federal features”. The unitary features tilt the balance of power in favour of the Centre, so India is a quasi-federation – a federal system with a very strong Centre.

107.s: How does the Preamble describe India?
107.x: The Preamble does not describe India as federal, unitary or quasi-federal – it says “Sovereign Socialist Secular Democratic Republic”.

107.s: Which scholar: The Constitution "avoids the tight mould of federalism" and "could be both unitary as well as federal according…?
107.x: B.R. Ambedkar – The Constitution "avoids the tight mould of federalism" and "could be both unitary as well as federal according to the requirements of time and circumstances"

107.s: Which scholar: Unitary bias grew from the financial dependence of States and the Planning Commission?
107.x: K. Santhanam – Unitary bias grew from the financial dependence of States and the Planning Commission

107.s: Which clause says "India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States"?
107.x: Art. 1(1) – “India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States” – the only names are India and Bharat

107.s: Where is the word "federation" used in the Constitution?
107.x: “Federation” – Nowhere used in the Constitution; India is described neither as a federation nor as a confederation

107.s: From which Act is the phrase "Union of States" taken?
107.x: “Union of States” – Taken from the British North America Act, 1867 (Canada)

107.s: Which right do Indian States not have, according to Ambedkar?
107.x: Ambedkar's two reasons – (i) The federation is not the result of an agreement among the States (unlike the USA); (ii) the States have no right to secede – the Union is indestructible

107.s: What kind of Union is India under Article 1?
107.x: Nature – An indissoluble Union of States – not formed at the will of States; cannot be dissolved by Parliament, State Assemblies or plebiscite

107.s: What majority does Parliament need under Art. 3 to alter a State's boundaries without its consent?
107.x: Indestructible Union of destructible States – Parliament can alter the area, boundaries or name of any State without its consent by a simple majority (Art. 3)

107.s: How is the USA described, as against India's destructible States?
107.x: USA – Indestructible Union of indestructible States

107.s: Which Amendment allowed free-speech restrictions in the interest of India's sovereignty and integrity?
107.x: Secession – No right of self-determination/secession; advocacy of secession is not protected by free speech – the 16th Amendment (1963) allows restrictions in the interest of sovereignty and integrity of India

107.s: Which term in Article 1 covers the States only, not the UTs?
107.x: Territory of India – States + UTs + acquired territories; “Union of India” = the States only; both in the First Schedule

107.s: Which Article provides for admitting new States not part of India?
107.x: Art. 2 – Admission/establishment of new States not part of India

107.s: Which Article says laws under Arts 2-3 are not Art. 368 amendments?
107.x: Art. 4 – Laws under Arts 2-3 changing the First and Fourth Schedules are not Art. 368 amendments

107.s: Whose recommendation does an Art. 3 Bill on new States need?
107.x: Art. 3 Bill – Needs the President's recommendation

107.s: With which Article does the Seventh Schedule distribute legislative powers?
107.x: Seventh Schedule (with Article 246, Part XI) – Distributes legislative powers/subjects between the Union and the States in three Lists – reflects the federal structure

107.s: When did the Seventh Schedule with its three Lists come into the Constitution?
107.x: Origin – Part of the original Constitution

107.s: Which Schedule lists the languages of India?
107.x: Other Schedules – Sixth = tribal areas of the North-East; Eighth = languages; Ninth = protected laws; Eleventh = Panchayats; Fifth = Scheduled Areas; Third = oaths

107.x: I – Union – Parliament – exclusive (Art. 246(1)) – 97 – 98

107.x: I – Union – Parliament – exclusive (Art. 246(1)) – 97 – 98

107.s: How many live entries does the Union List have now?
107.x: I – Union – Parliament – exclusive (Art. 246(1)) – 97 – 98

107.s: Under which clause do States legislate exclusively on the State List?
107.x: II – State – State Legislature – exclusive “in normal circumstances” (Art. 246(3)) – 66 – 59
