107.x: II – State – State Legislature – exclusive “in normal circumstances” (Art. 246(3)) – 66 – 59

107.s: How many live entries does the State List have now?
107.x: II – State – State Legislature – exclusive “in normal circumstances” (Art. 246(3)) – 66 – 59

107.s: Under which clause do both Parliament and States legislate on the Concurrent List?
107.x: III – Concurrent – Both Parliament and State Legislatures (Art. 246(2)) – 47 – 52

107.s: How many entries did the Concurrent List have originally?
107.x: III – Concurrent – Both Parliament and State Legislatures (Art. 246(2)) – 47 – 52

107.s: How many live entries does the Concurrent List have now?
107.x: III – Concurrent – Both Parliament and State Legislatures (Art. 246(2)) – 47 – 52

107.s: Which List has more subjects than the State List, making the Centre strong?
107.x: The Union List has more subjects than the State List – one reason the Centre is called strong. Numbering still ends at 97 / 66 / 47 because entries were inserted (e.g. Union Entry 92A, inter-State sales tax, by the 6th Amendment, 1956) or omitted.

107.s: Which Amendment inserted Union Entry 92A on inter-State sales tax?
107.x: The Union List has more subjects than the State List – one reason the Centre is called strong. Numbering still ends at 97 / 66 / 47 because entries were inserted (e.g. Union Entry 92A, inter-State sales tax, by the 6th Amendment, 1956) or omitted.

107.s: Which List prevails when entries in the three Lists overlap?
107.x: Precedence – Union List > Concurrent List > State List when entries overlap

107.s: When does a repugnant State law on a Concurrent subject prevail?
o: If reserved and assented by the President
107.x: Concurrent List conflict (Art. 254) – The Union law prevails – except a State law reserved for and assented to by the President, which prevails in that State (Art. 254(2)) until Parliament legislates again

107.s: Who can legislate on the Concurrent List?
107.x: Concurrent List – Both Parliament and the States legislate

107.s: Under which Article can Parliament legislate on the State List in the national interest?
107.x: State List – Parliament can legislate under special circumstances (Arts 249, 250, 252, 253, 356)

107.s: On which List's subjects are Central sector schemes mostly framed?
107.x: Central sector schemes – Mostly framed on Union List subjects

107.s: What happens to India's federal structure during an emergency?
107.x: Effect of an emergency – The Centre becomes all-powerful; the federal structure converts into a unitary one without a formal amendment – unique among federations

107.s: Which Amendment allowed a National Emergency for any part of India?
107.x: National Emergency (Art. 352) – Declared for all of India or any part (42nd Amendment); the only case where the Union assumes full legislative and executive control (President's Rule covers one State; ordinances or martial law (Art. 34) do not)

107.s: Which Articles of Part XVIII contain the Emergency provisions?
107.x: Place – Part XVIII (Arts 352-360); three kinds: National (352), State/President's Rule (356), Financial (360)

107.s: Under which Article can the Centre give executive directions to a State on any matter in an Emergency?
107.x: Art. 353 – The Centre can give executive directions to a State on any matter

107.s: How long at a time can Parliament legislate on a State subject under a Rajya Sabha resolution?
107.x: Rajya Sabha resolution (2/3 present and voting) in national interest → Parliament legislates on a State subject (1 year, renewable)

107.s: When do Parliament's laws on State subjects made in an Emergency lapse?
107.x: During a National Emergency Parliament legislates on the State List; laws lapse 6 months after it ends

107.s: Which Article lets Parliament legislate for two or more States at their request?
107.x: Two or more States request Parliament to legislate

107.s: Which Article empowers Parliament to legislate to implement international agreements?
107.x: Laws to implement international agreements

107.s: How long does a President's order cutting tax shares to States in an Emergency last?
o: End of the financial year the Emergency ends in
107.x: President may reduce or cancel (never increase) the transfer of finances – tax shares and grants – to the States during a National Emergency; the order lasts till the end of the financial year in which the Emergency ends

107.s: Which ground replaced "internal disturbance" for a National Emergency under the 44th Amendment?
107.x: Ground – War, external aggression, armed rebellion (44th replaced “internal disturbance”) – Failure of constitutional machinery – Threat to financial stability

107.s: What is the ground for imposing President's Rule?
107.x: Ground – War, external aggression, armed rebellion (44th replaced “internal disturbance”) – Failure of constitutional machinery – Threat to financial stability

107.s: What time and majority are needed to approve a National Emergency?
107.x: Approval – 1 month, special majority – 2 months, simple – 2 months, simple

107.s: What time does Parliament have to approve President's Rule?
107.x: Approval – 1 month, special majority – 2 months, simple – 2 months, simple

107.s: What time does Parliament have to approve a Financial Emergency?
107.x: Approval – 1 month, special majority – 2 months, simple – 2 months, simple

107.s: What is the maximum total duration of a National Emergency?
107.x: Duration – 6 months at a time, no maximum – 6 months at a time, max 3 years (beyond 1 year: National Emergency + EC certificate) – Until revoked

107.s: How long does a Financial Emergency last once approved?
107.x: Duration – 6 months at a time, no maximum – 6 months at a time, max 3 years (beyond 1 year: National Emergency + EC certificate) – Until revoked

107.s: Which Emergency has been used many times, including in AP in 1973?
107.x: Used – 3 times – 1962, 1971, 1975 – Many times (AP 1973, Jai Andhra) – Never

107.s: How many times has a Financial Emergency been declared?
107.x: Used – 3 times – 1962, 1971, 1975 – Many times (AP 1973, Jai Andhra) – Never

107.s: When did the 1962 Emergency on Chinese aggression end?
107.x: Chinese aggression (Oct; in force till Jan 1968) – external aggression

107.s: On which ground was the December 1971 Emergency declared?
107.x: Pakistan (Dec) – external aggression

107.s: When was the 1975 Emergency withdrawn?
107.x: Internal disturbance (made while the 1971 one was in force); 25 June 1975 – Samvidhan Hatya Diwas (25 June); withdrawn 21 March 1977

107.s: What share of Lok Sabha members can seek a sitting to disapprove an Emergency?
107.x: 44th Amendment (1978) – Cabinet's written advice; 1/10th of Lok Sabha members can seek a sitting to disapprove; Arts 20-21 never suspended; Art. 19 suspended automatically only in war/external aggression; the 38th Amendment had barred judicial review

107.s: Which Emergency alone affects Fundamental Rights?
107.x: Fundamental Rights – Only a National Emergency affects them; others suspended only by a Presidential order under Art. 359 (Art. 19 automatically under Art. 358 only in war/external aggression) – not all FRs

107.s: How long after an Emergency ends can an extended Lok Sabha term run at most?
107.x: Term of the House – Parliament can extend the Lok Sabha/Assembly term by 1 year at a time, at most 6 months after the Emergency ends

107.s: How many days after the new Lok Sabha's first sitting does a proclamation survive if the old House was dissolved?
107.x: New Lok Sabha – A proclamation survives 30 days after its first sitting if the old one was dissolved

107.s: What can the Centre order for judges' salaries during a Financial Emergency?
